figures.caption: Figure 1. Experimental design. (A) Participants were presented with polyphonic music made 195 of two monophonic streams (PolyOrig condition), with control stimuli where the average pitch 196 heights for the two streams were inverted (PolyInv), and with the corresponding monophonic 197 streams in isolation (Monophonic). All stimuli were synthesised from MIDI scores using high 198 quality virtual piano sounds. (B) Each experimental session was organised into two blocks: a 199 listening block, where EEG signals were recorded from participants during uninstructed music 200 listening, followed by a music identification block. The music pieces were selected randomly 201 from any condition, an a given piece was presented once, only in one of the three conditions, 202 without repetitions. In the melody identification block, participants heard short polyphonic 203 snippet from the same pieces, and were asked to sing back the melody and to indicate if that 204 was the high or low pitch stream on a five-point scale. This led to a behavioural measurement 205 of attention bias. (C) Attention bias was also measured from the neural signal. Attention 206 decoding models were built on the monophonic condition, by fitting backward temporal 207 response functions (TRF) on each participant to reconstruct the sound envelope from the EEG 208 signal. TRF models were then applied to the polyphonic conditions to decode the attended 209 melody, resulting in a neural measurement of attention bias. 210

Figure 2. Behavioural and neural indices of attention bias during uninstructed listening 269 of polyphonic music. (A) Illustration of the hypothesised attention bias scenarios for 270 polyphonic music listening. A high-pitch bias was expected for PolyOrig by design. Dominant 271 high-voice superiority effect or motif attractiveness were expected to lead to a strong attention 272 bias toward the high (Hp0) and low (Hp2) pitch streams respectively, while a substantial 273 reduction in attention bias would reflect a comparable contribution of the two factors (Hp1). 274 (B) Behavioural result. The behavioural attention bias metric (mean ± SEM; ***p<0.001) was 275 derived from the subjective reporting in the melody identification block. Subjective ratings 276 indicated what stream was perceived as the main melody, from value -2 (low pitch) to value 2 277 (high pitch). (C) EEG decoding analysis. (Left) Envelope reconstruction correlations for the 278 decoding analysis are reported (mean ± SEM; *p<0.05, ***p<0.001) for individual streams 279 (high and low pitch) and conditions (PolyOrig and PolyInv). Colours refer to the motif (red: 280 main melody; blue: support stream). Note that colours are inverted in the two conditions, 281 reflecting the pitch inversion. (Right) Envelope reconstruction correlations for individual 282 participants. (D) Neural attention bias index, which was obtained by subtracting the high and 283 low pitch reconstruction correlations in (C) within each condition (Δcorrelation; mean ± SEM; 284 **p<0.01). Figure 3. Low-frequency cortical encoding of melodic expectation during polyphonic 364 music listening. (A) Schematics of the analysis method. Canonical Correlation Analysis 365 (CCA) was run to study the stimulus-EEG relationship. Match-vs-mismatch classification 366 scores were derived to quantify the strength of the neural encoding of a given stimulus feature-367 set. (B) The analysis was run separately for acoustic-only features (A) and acoustic+melodic 368 expectations features (AM) in each of the three experimental conditions. The distributions in 369 the figure indicate repetitions of the match-vs-mismatch procedure. (C) The gain in match-vs-370 mismatch classification after including the melodic expectation features, ΔClassification, is 371 compared across conditions and models, informing on whether a monophonic or a polyphonic 372 account of melodic expectations best fit the neural data. In the box-plot, the bottom and top 373 edges mark the 25th and 75th percentiles respectively, while the mid-line indicates the median 374 value (***p<0.001). 375
